mappings.note: Cellulose against chitin as the wall material separating Plantae from Fungi -- a cellular-organisation characteristic, C-4.1-LO-1. Not C-4.1-LO-2: both kingdoms are named in the question, so nothing is being placed.

Bryophytes on land but still needing free water for their gametes -- the incomplete land transition of a plant division, which this curriculum houses only under the C4.2 competency. Not C4.5: the item explains a constraint on the group, it does not argue an evolutionary advance.

What xylem and phloem do for a pteridophyte -- the tissue level serving a larger body, C4.2. Shares the plant-division family's single home; there is no plant equivalent of C4.2-LO-5 to separate these items with.

WEAK FIT: naked seeds on cones against seeds enclosed in fruit is a REPRODUCTIVE contrast, and curriculum 82 has no outcome for plant reproduction or seed structure. C4.2 is cited as the nearest home; C4.5 was rejected because the item states a difference and makes no adaptive argument.
A symbiosis named and explained: alga feeds, fungus shelters. LO-15 names lichens outright, which makes it the single precise row for this item and for the other lichen items in the chapter.

Defines the notochord as the flexible rod that precedes the vertebral column -- the criterion LO-5 is used with to place an animal among the chordates. No chordate-specific outcome exists to prefer over it.

Bilateral symmetry against the asymmetry of sponges -- body organisation used to separate two phyla, LO-5. NOT C4.2-LO-6 despite Porifera appearing: LO-6's contrast partner is Cnidaria and its subject is the tissue level, whereas the discriminator here is symmetry.

What the exoskeleton buys an arthropod -- protection, water retention, muscle attachment. Adaptive function, C4.5, consistent with the other two exoskeleton items. Arthropoda has no outcome of its own, which is why these do not sit with the phylum-placement items on C4.2-LO-5.

The defining feature of Annelida stated as segmentation plus the flexibility and precise locomotion it allows -- both halves of LO-7. The one animal phylum in this chapter whose recall item lands exactly on its own outcome.
A calcium carbonate endoskeleton supporting an animal that has no notochord -- internal body organisation used to characterise Echinodermata, LO-5. Echinodermata has no row of its own.

POOR FIT: listing Kingdom to Species in order is pure rank hierarchy, which curriculum 82 does not cover for this chapter. C-4.1-LO-2 is cited for 'classify organisms in groups' alone, and this is the barest of the hierarchy items -- nothing but the seven names is asked.
Why binomial nomenclature was introduced -- avoiding the confusion of regional common names, which is the 'significance' half of LO-3.

One RULE for writing a scientific name (italics in print, underlined by hand) -- the 'rules' half of LO-3. Worth recording that LO-3 fuses significance and rules into one row, so this item and the 'why was it introduced' item above cannot be told apart by code however differently they are marked.

Woese, 1977, and DNA as the basis -- a straight statement of the current understanding, C7.1. Deliberately NOT paired with C4.2-LO-9 as the three-domain multiple-choice item was: that one tests that Monera is no longer a top-level group, engaging the succession of kingdom systems, while this one asks only who and on what evidence.

Fossils as the record of simple ancient forms becoming complex modern ones -- C4.5's 'evidences of biological evolution'. Not C2.8: rock layers appear as a timeline, not as an Earth process being studied.

Dependent organisms suffering when one species goes -- interactions between groups of organisms, LO-15. Same reading as the multiple-choice version of this question; the ecological balance in the answer follows from the interaction rather than being the object of the item.

Abundant wildlife providing alternative hosts and so diluting infection -- a between-group interaction, LO-15. Not C2.8 alone: the mechanism named is host-to-host, and the item never widens to the forest as an Earth system the way the three-statement disaster item does.

The Purple Frog find framed as evidence that conservation is urgent -- C5.2, whose example list includes conservation of biodiversity. Not C4.5: the frog's ancient lineage is mentioned, but the item asks for the significance of the discovery, which is a conservation argument.

Hotspots explained with Indian examples, including the habitat-loss half of the definition and the conservation case it makes -- C5.2. Endemism appears here only as the ingredient, so not C2.8, which is where the bare endemism items sit.

Defines classification and then names two benefits of it -- the grouping verb of C-4.1-LO-2, extended. Not C-4.1-LO-3: the benefits given are organised study and evolutionary relationships, not naming, so the nomenclature outcome does not reach it.

The five-kingdom split drawn as a flowchart on cell type and body organisation (C-4.1-LO-2), with an explicit representation demand that LO-27 covers -- 'Represent findings in multiple modes, including appropriate figures'. The second half, why Monera stands apart, stays inside LO-2's criteria rather than reaching C4.2-LO-9, since no system change is discussed.

Refuting the claim needs a third multicellular eukaryotic kingdom to be placed (Fungi, C-4.1-LO-2) and then justified on chitin walls and absorptive nutrition (C-4.1-LO-1). Both halves are marked, so both are cited.

A straight Monera-against-Protista comparison on cell type and body organisation -- the distinguishing characteristics of C-4.1-LO-1. Not C-4.1-LO-2: both kingdoms are named in the question, so no placement is performed.

Fungi as decomposers, explained through saprophytic nutrition and nutrient return -- the 'ecological role' clause of C-4.1-LO-2, the same row as the short fungal-decomposer item. This curriculum has one outcome for what a kingdom does in an ecosystem and both belong on it.

Two explicit asks: name the kingdom from the illustration (Protista, C-4.1-LO-2) and state the cellular feature that justifies it (a true nucleus in a single cell, C-4.1-LO-1). The justification clause is what earns the second code here and not on the other identify-the-kingdom items.
